Instructions

In this study you will read 6 short scenarios. For each scenario, you will be asked to rate some statements about the scenario and people involved. The questions will appear on multiple pages, but the story will always be shown at the top of all pages.

In some of the questions, you will be asked to report a single value on a slider to indicate the answer you think is most likely. For example, if you think 2 is more likely than any other number on the scale, slide the slider knob to the number 2. However, if you really think there is not a single value that is more likely than others, you can choose the option “I don’t know. All values are equally likely”. If you choose this option, you don’t need to move the slider knob to choose a value.

Although the 6 sets of scenarios and questions follow a similar structure, we would appreciate if you try to consider each scenario on its own, and make judgements based on the information in that scenario alone.

Important: For each scenario, there is a set of questions that will be repeated four times. However, each time you will answer these questions after reading about a different piece of information in the story. So, this is not a glitch in the survey, please pay attention to the information that is provided each time. This information will be written in bold so that you can find it more easily. The rest of the scenario will not change.
